topic: Input Stream Iterators and Equality Comparison in C++
explanation: In C++, input stream iterators (std::istream_iterator) are used to read data from input streams such as std::cin in a way that integrates seamlessly with the Standard Template Library algorithms. They are designed to facilitate reading sequences of data lazily and efficiently. Two istream iterators are considered equal if they both reach the end of the stream (end-of-stream iterators) or if they are pointing to the same position in the stream, enabling comparison operations that control iteration flow in generic algorithms.
